title: React Server Components: The Philosophy
description: Deeply understand what Server Components are, why they exist, and how they change the component mental model.

slides.title: The Two Component Types 🧩
slides.content:
# A New Mental Model

In the Next.js App Router, components are **either** Server Components or Client Components.

* **Server Components** – render only on the server. Never sent to the client as JavaScript. Can directly access databases, files, secrets.
* **Client Components** – rendered on the server (for initial HTML) and in the browser. They have interactivity (useState, useEffect, onClick).

All components are Server Components by default. You opt into Client Components by adding `'use client'` at the top of the file.

Analogy: Server Components are the chef preparing the meal; Client Components are the waiter adding the final touch at the table. 🍽️

slides.title: Server Component Example (app/page.js)
slides.content: This component runs on the server, fetches data, and sends ready‑made HTML.

quizData.question: In the App Router, what is the default type of a new component?
quizData.explanation: Every component in the App Router is a Server Component unless you add the `'use client'` directive at the top of the file.

slides.title: The Server‑Only Power 🧠
slides.content:
# What Server Components Can Do

* Access databases directly (no API route needed).
* Read the filesystem.
* Use Node.js built‑ins.
* Keep large dependencies on the server (zero client bundle impact).
* Fetch data at the component level.

They **cannot** use state, effects, or browser‑only APIs.

This means your heavy markdown parser or database query never reaches the user's browser.

slides.title: Client Component Example (components/Counter.js)

quizData.question: A Server Component can be imported and used inside a Client Component in which way?

options.text: Directly as a child passed via props (composition pattern)
By importing and rendering it normally
Server Components can't appear inside Client Components at all
Only if it's wrapped in Suspense

quizData.explanation: You cannot import a Server Component into a Client Component file. However, you can pass a Server Component as `children` or via a prop from a parent Server Component. This is the allowed interleaving.

slides.title: The Interleaving Rule ↔️
slides.content:
# The Golden Rule of RSC Composition

* A Server Component can import and render both Server and Client Components.
* A Client Component can import and render only other Client Components (and some third‑party components that are client‑side).
* To use a Server Component inside a Client Component, pass it as `children` from a Server Component parent.

This ensures that the server‑side code stays on the server, and the client bundle stays minimal.

slides.title: Composition Pattern (app/layout.js and app/page.js)
slides.content: Server Component passes a Server Component as children to a Client Component.

quizData.question: How can you safely include a Server Component inside a Client Component?

options.text: Import it directly in the Client Component file
Pass it as `children` from a parent Server Component

quizData.explanation: The parent Server Component renders the Client Component and places the Server Component inside via children or props. The boundary prevents the server code from entering the client bundle.

slides.title: Why This Matters 🚀
slides.content: Server Components can reduce your client‑side JavaScript dramatically. A complex component with a heavy library (e.g., syntax highlighter) can stay entirely on the server, sending only the highlighted HTML to the client.
